questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Most important was academic opportunities. However, practicality also played a role, where I at University of Toronto (UofT) was able to find two courses replacing mandatory courses for my degree.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: University of Toronto and the city of Toronto was overall a good place for studying abroad. I was able to find very interesting courses, there was many exchange students at UofT hence many opportunities to socialize and Toronto was a nice city to live in. My overall rating of the stay is influenced negatively by the limitations because of Covid-19 during the stay and the different educational system.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The only information, which was difficult to find (changing a lot) was information regarding Covid-19 travel restrictions to Canada.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The inbound exchange office provided us with the necessary information regarding the academics and to some extent Covid-19 restrictions. Unfortunately, because of Covid-19 was orientation online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any difficulties finding housing on my own in Toronto. Because of the pandemic and the uncertainty, I found housing after arriving to Canada. Facebook Marketplace was very useful, and I was invited to around 5-7 viewings and was able to find a place within a week. I can therefore recommend Facebook Marketplace. Being able to go to viewings was very helpful and a good way to see different parts of the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was able to find housing around a 15 min. walk from Campus (St. George), but Campus is very large and thus you can easily spend an additional 15 min. walking on Campus to get to your specific location. I didn't find the TTC (Public transportation) very reliable and preferred walking. I was happy about living in downtown Toronto since many of the social events (Both general and with the other exchange students) was in this area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Regarding housing to students: Many of the dorms I looked at was expensive and therefore not something I looked further into.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The inbound exchange office provided us with all the necessary information regarding course registration.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: From what I remember, the inbound exchange office email us google forms we used to apply for the courses. I think there was in total 3 applications rounds, since it is not certain that you will receive all the courses you applied for in a given round.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All the relevant information was provided by the inbound exchange office, and I didn't needed additional information/ help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite lucky and was able to get 4 out of 5 courses I applied for in the first round. The only course I didn't get was cancelled. However, two of the courses had waitlists with +200 students and therefore very sought after, which is the reason I feel quite lucky with the registration process. In the second round I applied for my final course and was placed on the waiting list. I got into the course before the start of the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply as soon as you get the google forms from the inbound exchange office. Additionally, I prepared documents with course descriptions from KU translated to justify having the necessary prerequisites. From what I remember they were quite strict in relation to prerequisites. Finally apply for as many courses in the first round as possible. You can always drop courses afterwards.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I feel the courses in general had a lower theoretical level compared to UCPH but then covered more topics.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different and quite difficult going from normally focusing on two courses to have five courses simultaneously. Furthermore, the courses in general had many elements contributing to the final grade in forms of discussions, assignments, midterms, final exam, group projects or quizzes. In one of the courses, I had in total 28 elements contributing to the final grade. The intensity of the semester and overall workload was therefore higher at UofT. I feel the teaching style reminded me more of the teaching style in gymnasium rather than at UCPH. My feeling from group projects, lectures, and discussions with other students in the courses was that they were a lot more focused on grades rather than learning the topics/theory covered. Likewise, I sometimes had the feeling that the lectures were too focused on the final exam/ assignments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
APM236: Application of Linear Programming
ECO326: Advanced Economic Theory, Game Theory 
STA302: Method of Data Analysis 1
STA314: Statistical Methods for Machine Learning 1
ECO372: Data Analysis and Applied Econometrics in Practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I was able to have APM236 replace OR1 and ECO326 replace MikØk2. However, the courses I enjoyed the most was the three other courses. In general, for all 5 courses the professor was very good at teaching and communicating their knowledge. 

STA314 covered both supervised and unsupervised machine learning. The pace of the course was very intense, and the course covered a lot of algorithms: K-NN, decision trees, linear regression, logistic regression, ensembles, SVMs, PCA, K-means and probabilistic models. And general methods: maximum likelihood, entropy, optimization with gradient descent and stochastic gradient descent, and Bayesian inference. The implementing part of the course is doable, but I spend quite some time on the assignments with python programming. 

STA302 is in the beginning covering theory of linear regression, which I had before in previous courses but in the end introduce topics like Box-Cox transformation of variables, Akaike Information Criterion, Bayesian Information Criterion, backwards selection, forwards selection and stepwise selection within linear regression. Finally, is the focus more practical and I wrote a final report using the IMRAD structure, which I think is a good exercise before a bachelor thesis.

ECO372 focussed on when you can conclude causality from observational data in an economic setting. The course introduced first the Rubin causal model, which is a framework using potential outcomes to estimate causal effects. In the end of the course, the lectures also covered some of the methods developed by Angrist and Imbens for which they received a Nobel price in Economics in 2021. The course was interesting because it focused on many recent research papers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to travel to Stockholm to get the student visa, which was unexpected. No other major unexpected costs related to the exchange but the cost of travelling round Canada was a bit higher than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in groceries stores was more expensive than expected but eating out was a bit less expensive than expected. Getting a Canadian phone plan was also expensive, and I ended using my Danish phone plan with international coverage.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because of Covid-19, there was limited tickets for the club's fair, and I was unfortunately late and therefore not able to get one. I was therefore not introduced to the clubs and from the online information was it difficult to see if the club was still active. I therefore didn't used any of the non-academic opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Explained in the previous comment.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend socializing with the other exchange students. There was many other exchange students and I enjoyed socializing with many interesting people from all over the world.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed exploring Toronto, which have many things to offer. I went to a couple of NBA games and really liked the atmosphere. Toronto is also very diverse, and you can therefore find many interesting places to eat or grab a drink. I can also recommend attending Toronto International Film Festival. Finally, going out on road trips was also very nice and Canada/Ontario has a lot of nice places. I can recommend Algonquin Park, Bruce Peninsula National Park and Killarney Provincial Park.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any difficulties at all.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I socialized mostly with other exchange students. I feel like Covid-19 limited socializing with many of the local students e.g. part of the lectures was online and restrictions on campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity in Toronto!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be good at prioritizing, since it was difficult to balance both socializing with exchange students and following the interesting courses. Go out on road trips away from Toronto and experience some of the local culture and amazing nature.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not additional to what I have already wrote.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Interesting courses and the relationships with some of the other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid-19.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
